IN_PROGRESS.description: Chunks remain; NEXT_OFFSET is where the next read starts.

COMPLETE.description: The source was read to its end and every chunk was committed. NEXT_OFFSET equals the total length when the length is known.

FAILED.description: The publisher stopped on an error it did not recover from; FAULT states what happened. The mark stays valid as a resume point.

ABANDONED.description: The publisher abandoned the job deliberately; it is not a resume point and a consumer restarts from offset 0.

INVALIDATED.description: The source changed identity underneath the job (VALIDATOR mismatch), so the position no longer refers to the same bytes. A conforming consumer restarts from offset 0 rather than resuming.

OFFSET_LENGTH.description: Half-open ranges expressed as a start offset and a byte count.

INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE.description: Inclusive first/last byte positions, the convention of ranged transfer protocols: a chunk of `RANGE_FIRST_BYTE`..`RANGE_LAST_BYTE` inclusive.

PART_INDEX.description: The source is delivered as discrete numbered parts and byte offsets are not addressable; CHUNK_INDEX is the only position.

MATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they agree; resuming is safe.

MISMATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they disagree; the bytes behind the offset are not the bytes that were read.

UNVERIFIABLE.description: The source published no validator to compare. This is NOT a match: a publisher that cannot verify identity says so instead of assuming it.

IRMSource.description:
The source object a job is reading, and the validators that prove a resumed
read is reading the same bytes.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable locator of the source object, verbatim.

SOURCE_OBJECT_ID.description:
Source-native object, export, or product identifier verbatim, when the
provider names one independently of its locator.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier pinning the exact source bytes, when the source is
content-addressed.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: Media type of the source object verbatim as the provider states it.

TOTAL_BYTES.description:
Total length of the source object in bytes. 0 means the provider did not
state a length; it never means an empty object.

ENTITY_TAG.description: Opaque entity validator verbatim as the provider published it.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the complete source object as 64 lowercase hexadecimal
characters, when the provider publishes one. Never computed from a partial
read.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: Provider-stated edition, revision, or release marker verbatim.

VALIDATOR_MATCH.description: What the publisher concluded when it last compared validators.

MATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they agree; resuming is safe.

MISMATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they disagree; the bytes behind the offset are not the bytes that were read.

UNVERIFIABLE.description: The source published no validator to compare. This is NOT a match: a publisher that cannot verify identity says so instead of assuming it.

VALIDATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of that comparison.

IRMDecodeContext.description:
Everything a resuming reader needs to decode a chunk that does not begin at
offset 0. Required whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header.

FORMAT.description:
Format token the decoder dispatches on, verbatim and lowercase, e.g.
`text/csv`. A consumer that does not implement the format refuses the chunk
rather than guessing at a layout.

HEADER_LINE.description:
The source's header line verbatim, exactly as it appeared at offset 0 and
excluding its line terminator. This is the field that makes chunk N>0
decodable; without it a headerless chunk parses to zero rows and looks like
a clean tail.

HEADER_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length the header occupied at the start of the source, including its
terminator, so a reader can tell a header-bearing prefix from a data row.

COLUMN_NAMES.description:
Column names in source order, when the publisher parsed them. Advisory:
HEADER_LINE is authoritative and a disagreement is resolved in its favour.

CHARSET.description: Character encoding label verbatim as the provider states it.

COMPRESSION.description:
Stream-compression codec applied to the source bytes, verbatim and
lowercase. Empty means the ranged bytes are read as-is. Non-empty means
NEXT_OFFSET is a position in the COMPRESSED stream and DECODER_STATE,
WINDOW and PARTIAL_RECORD are all required to resume.

DECODED_OFFSET.description:
Position in the DECODED stream corresponding to NEXT_OFFSET, when the
source is compressed. 0 with a non-empty COMPRESSION means the decoded
stream has not been advanced.

DECODER_STATE.description:
Serialized, pointer-free image of the decoder at the seam — the state a
codec with no restart point needs in order to have one. Opaque to every
consumer but a decoder whose stamps match exactly. Never partially applied.

DECODER_STATE_FORMAT.description:
Layout identifier of DECODER_STATE, verbatim, naming the decoder struct the
image was taken from. A consumer that does not know the token restarts.

DECODER_STATE_VERSION.description: Version of that layout, verbatim. Any disagreement restarts the job.

DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length DECODER_STATE is expected to have. Carried even though the
vector knows its own size, so a size disagreement is detectable BEFORE the
image is loaded into a differently shaped struct.

DECODER_STATE_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of DECODER_STATE as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

DECODER_BUILD_ID.description:
Build identifier of the decoder that produced DECODER_STATE, verbatim, so
two builds of one codec version are still distinguishable.

DECODER_STATE_MEDIA_TYPE.description:
Media type of DECODER_STATE, so an unrelated decoder refuses it instead of
misreading it.

WINDOW.description:
The decoder's history window at the seam — the bytes that ARE the codec's
back-reference dictionary. Carried separately from DECODER_STATE because it
is bulk data of a size the codec fixes, not part of the struct image.

WINDOW_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length WINDOW is expected to have, for the same detect-before-load
reason as DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.

WINDOW_POSITION.description:
Offset into WINDOW at which the codec will next write, when the window is
a circular buffer whose contents cannot be interpreted without it.

PARTIAL_RECORD.description:
The bytes of the record that straddles the seam: everything the previous
chunk decoded of a record it could not finish. A resuming decoder prepends
these to the next chunk's decoded output before parsing. Carried as bytes,
not text, because a seam may fall inside a multi-byte character.

IRMChunk.description: One chunk that was read and durably committed.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based position of the chunk in the job's read sequence.

BATCH_ID.description:
Publisher-stable batch identifier the chunk's records were stored under,
verbatim, so a consumer can join the mark to the stored rows.

RANGE_FIRST_BYTE.description: First byte of the range that was read.

RANGE_LAST_BYTE.description:
Last byte of the range that was read. Interpreted per RANGE_MODE:
inclusive under INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE, exclusive under OFFSET_LENGTH.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Bytes the read actually returned, which may be shorter than the range
requested.

CHUNK_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of the chunk's bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

RECORDS_DECODED.description: Records the decoder produced from the chunk.

RECORDS_STORED.description:
Records the storage lane reported as durably committed. A chunk whose
stored count is 0 is not marked at all.

RECORDS_REJECTED.description: Records the storage lane rejected or collapsed as duplicates.

ATTEMPTS.description: Number of read attempts this chunk cost, including the successful one.

COMMITTED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the storage lane
confirmed the commit.

IRMFault.description: The last unrecovered error, carried so a resumed run can refuse to loop.

MESSAGE.description: Human-readable message verbatim; never a substitute for CODE.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based index of the chunk the fault occurred on.

CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.description: Consecutive failed attempts at that chunk.

OCCURRED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of the fault.

RETRY_NOT_BEFORE.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp before which a consumer must not
retry. Empty means the publisher states no backoff.

JOB_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the ingest job. Together with the publishing
key it is the job's identity across every mark it emits.

SEQUENCE.description:
Monotonic version of this mark within JOB_ID. Highest wins per publishing
key. Never reused, never decremented.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the data provider being read, verbatim.
Publisher data: it may name a real provider.

INGESTOR_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS identifier of the ingest module or flow that owns the job, so
two pipelines reading one provider do not share a resume point.

SOURCE.description: The source object and its validators.

IN_PROGRESS.description: Chunks remain; NEXT_OFFSET is where the next read starts.

COMPLETE.description: The source was read to its end and every chunk was committed. NEXT_OFFSET equals the total length when the length is known.

FAILED.description: The publisher stopped on an error it did not recover from; FAULT states what happened. The mark stays valid as a resume point.

ABANDONED.description: The publisher abandoned the job deliberately; it is not a resume point and a consumer restarts from offset 0.

INVALIDATED.description: The source changed identity underneath the job (VALIDATOR mismatch), so the position no longer refers to the same bytes. A conforming consumer restarts from offset 0 rather than resuming.

RANGE_MODE.description: How byte positions in this mark are addressed.

OFFSET_LENGTH.description: Half-open ranges expressed as a start offset and a byte count.

INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE.description: Inclusive first/last byte positions, the convention of ranged transfer protocols: a chunk of `RANGE_FIRST_BYTE`..`RANGE_LAST_BYTE` inclusive.

PART_INDEX.description: The source is delivered as discrete numbered parts and byte offsets are not addressable; CHUNK_INDEX is the only position.

NEXT_OFFSET.description:
Byte offset at which the next read begins, in the SOURCE's own byte stream:
the compressed stream when DECODE_CONTEXT.COMPRESSION is non-empty, in
which case it is a record boundary only in company with the decoder state,
window and partial record. On an uncompressed source it is ALWAYS a
complete-record boundary, corrected backwards from the previous chunk's
byte budget. 0 is a valid value and means the job has committed nothing yet.

NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX.description:
Zero-based index of the next chunk to read. With PART_INDEX addressing this
is the only position.

CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET.description:
Byte budget the publisher reads per chunk. Records the ceiling the job
actually ran under, which a host may have clamped below the configured one.

DECODE_CONTEXT.description:
Everything needed to decode the chunk at NEXT_OFFSET. REQUIRED in practice
whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header; a consumer that finds
it absent there restarts from offset 0 rather than decoding blind.

LAST_CHUNK.description: The chunk this mark was advanced from — the last one durably committed.

CHUNKS_COMMITTED.description: Chunks durably committed by this job so far.

BYTES_COMMITTED.description: Source bytes accounted for by committed chunks.

RECORDS_COMMITTED.description: Records durably committed by this job so far, across every chunk.

TARGET_STANDARD.description:
Four-character standard code of the records this job writes, `$` included,
e.g. `$TBS`. Never a union ordinal.

RECONCILE_MODE.description:
Reconciliation mode the storage lane was called with, verbatim, e.g.
`append`. A chunked job never reconciles per batch: reconciling would delete
every earlier chunk as the next one arrived.

MERGE_POLICY.description: Deduplication or merge policy the job applied, verbatim.

FAULT.description: The last unrecovered error, when there is one.

CREATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job was created.

STARTED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the first chunk was read.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which this mark was published.
With JOB_ID and SEQUENCE this is the version key; SEQUENCE breaks ties.

COMPLETED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job reached COMPLETE.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp after which a consumer treats the
mark as stale and re-validates the source before resuming. Empty means the
publisher states no expiry.

TAGS.description: `namespace:value` facets, sorted and deduplicated. See TAG GRAMMAR above.

NOTES.description: Publisher note about this job; never a substitute for a field.
